native_ownership.responsibility: Produce a read-only, auditable AI cost model covering every billed workflow leg, exact/estimated/missing usage, uncertainty, sensitivity and product/margin controls.
excludes: Production usage metering, quota and credit settlement are owned by ai-product-operations.
General system performance optimization is owned by performance.
Implementation of model streaming is owned by ai-streaming.

risk.rationale: ai-cost-modeling produces diagnosis, design, or economic analysis only and must not modify repository or external state.

positive.prompt: Estimate per-run, tail-user and monthly cost for a RAG agent with cached and uncached input, embeddings, reranking, multiple tool/model rounds, retries, fallbacks and missing provider usage; show uncertainty and margin sensitivity.

Reconcile an AI feature's observed spend where some usage fields are null, retries share request identities and cached-token discounts are inconsistently reported. Produce lower/upper bounds and data-quality actions without changing production.

negative.prompt: Implement production AI usage events, atomic quota reservation and settlement, fallback attribution, reconciliation, dashboards and deterministic rollback controls.
Profile and optimize frontend/backend latency, database queries, CPU/memory, caching and capacity using measured performance evidence.

scenarios.prompt: Estimate a support agent's cost from logs that contain one initial call, cached-input fields, two tool round trips, a fallback retry and null usage on the final provider response. The existing spreadsheet treats null as zero and counts only the first prompt/completion.

assertions.criterion: Remains read-only and owns economic estimation/reconciliation while leaving runtime metering and implementation to neighboring skills.
Uses fixture/provider evidence for request identities, served models, pricing dates, token/usage exactness, cache eligibility, retries, tools and traffic without inventing missing values.
Defines the unit, enumerates every billed leg, labels exact/estimated/missing inputs, verifies live rates and units, then computes ranges and sensitivity before recommendations.

Counts cached and uncached input according to provider-confirmed usage, output/reasoning, every retry/fallback/tool model round, embeddings/reranking and non-token costs; treats null/missing usage as unresolved lower-bound spend, never zero.

Recalculates dimensions and request reconciliation, prevents duplicate/drop across retries, compares tail/high-usage and cache-miss scenarios and reconciles estimates to provider invoices where available.
Reports dated pricing sources, auditable assumptions, per-unit/monthly/tail ranges, lower-bound coverage, drivers, controls and uncertainty.
Separates provider rate inputs from formulas and avoids persisting remembered prices, cache discounts or universal usage thresholds.

scenarios.prompt: Finance asks for a margin report before launch, but a large share of provider usage is null and tool-runtime charges are unavailable. Explain what can be reported safely.

assertions.criterion: Does not mutate billing or publish a falsely complete number; labels missing coverage, exact decision scope and approval needed for any pricing or plan-limit consequence.
Reports observed spend only as a lower bound, models defensible ranges and separately identifies missing provider/tool legs instead of zero-filling.
Requires unit checks, request/invoice reconciliation and sensitivity showing whether the business decision changes under plausible missing-cost bounds.

scenarios.prompt: The selected provider changed current model prices and cached-input billing after an older estimate was written. Recalculate without embedding a remembered rate in the skill.

assertions.criterion: Requires current official provider pricing and billing definitions for the exact date/model/region/tier before a precise recalculation; when retrieval or those inputs are unavailable, refuses false precision and reports the evidence gap. Historical rates are used only for their matching measured period.

Matches the served model/version, usage fields, cache semantics, currency and billing period to applicable provider documentation or invoice when those sources are available, and otherwise identifies each missing input without inventing it.
Keeps volatile rates in cited task inputs or configuration rather than skill text and labels any unsupported provider field assumption.
